Ctrl + I: This shortcut italicizes selected text.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements about MS Word keyboard shortcuts is/are correct?

I. Ctrl + L aligns the selected text to the left, while Ctrl + E centers it

II. Ctrl + I and Ctrl + U can be used together to apply both italic and underline formatting simultaneously
questions.solution_en:
Both statements are true.

Ctrl + L and Ctrl + E are standard alignment shortcuts in Word, with Ctrl + L aligning text to the left and Ctrl + E centering it. These are part of the basic text formatting shortcuts.

The formatting shortcuts Ctrl + I (italic) and Ctrl + U (underline) can indeed be used in combination - you can press one after the other to apply both formats to the selected text. This is because Word allows multiple formatting attributes to be applied simultaneously to the same text.

Identify the correct statement(s) about Excel keyboard shortcuts:

I. Alt + Enter creates a new line within the same cell

II. F4 repeats the last action performed in Excel, while Ctrl + Y undoes the last action
questions.solution_en:
Alt + Enter is indeed used to create a new line within the same cell in Excel - this is essential for formatting text within cells without creating a new row. This statement is true.

The second statement is false. Both F4 and Ctrl + Y actually repeat the last action in Excel. Ctrl + Z (not Ctrl + Y) is the shortcut that undoes the last action.

questions.q_en:
Regarding PowerPoint keyboard shortcuts, which statement(s) is/are correct?

I. F5 starts the presentation from the beginning, while Shift + F5 starts from the current slide

II. The shortcut Alt + H + F + F will open the fonts dropdown menu
questions.solution_en:
Both statements are correct. F5 is the standard shortcut to start a presentation from the first slide, while Shift + F5 starts from the current slide - these are essential shortcuts for presenting efficiently.

The sequence Alt + H + F + F is indeed the correct keyboard sequence to access the fonts dropdown menu. This is part of PowerPoint's KeyTips system, where Alt reveals keyboard shortcuts for ribbon commands, and subsequent key presses navigate through the menu options (H for Home tab, F for Font group, F for Font dropdown).
